## Information about the nametags from Paul Lewis:
The labels in Scribus are 4 inches wide by 3 inches high. I got 4 labels per page in landscape orientation. The first name is in 42-point font and the last name (below the first name) is in 36 point font. At the top is a header that says "MBL Workshop on Molecular Evolution 2026" (12 point font) and on the bottom is a footer (12 point font) that has the name of the institution of the participant. I think I have an old Adobe InDesign template; if you use Adobe, let me know.

**Note after 2026:** The nametags holders we have are smaller than 4x3. We need to change this script to print labels 3x2, not 4x3. We might need to change the font size too.

US Letter in landscape is probably the cleanest here. You can fit a perfect grid of:

- 2 columns
- 3 rows
- 6 badges/page

with comfortable margins.

Below is a complete R script that:

- reads your CSV
- creates a duplex-ready PDF
- places 6 name tags per sheet
- creates matching back pages with mirrored placement
- uses 4" × 3" badges
- centers all text
- wraps long affiliations
- optionally draws cut borders

The output is designed for:

- duplex printing
- flip on short edge
- then cut with a paper cutter.

Your CSV should contain columns:

- `first_name`
- `last_name`
- `affiliation`
- `ip_address`

Note that all the IP addresses are in the `all-vm-ips.sh` file in `late-additions` folder from Paul. I copied this into a txt file, read into Excel and modified manually the columns for the faculty. I divided faculty+TAs and students in two sheets, and first worked manually on the faculty. I needed to add the Affiliation.
Actually, I had to manually change the students too based on the intro slides to use their preferred name.

We save the xls into two csv: faculty.csv and students.csv.

```{r}
source("generate_nametags.R")

# ── Entry point: set your paths here, then source or run the whole script ─────

csv_path   <- "faculty.csv"   # path to your CSV file
output_dir <- "faculty_nametags_output"    # folder where the PDF will be saved

csv_path   <- "students.csv"   # path to your CSV file
output_dir <- "students_nametags_output"    # folder where the PDF will be saved

generate_nametags(csv_path, output_dir)
```

**Instructions for printing:**

If your printer supports duplex printing:
- Set it to "Flip on short edge" (sometimes called "landscape duplex" or "tumble"). This is the setting that matches how the backs are mirrored in the PDF.
- Do not use "Flip on long edge" — that will misalign the backs.

If you're printing manually (single-sided printer):
- Print odd pages only (the fronts) first
- Take the printed sheets out and flip them along the short edge (the left/right side, not top/bottom) before re-feeding
- Print even pages only (the backs)
